company_name: CGI Inc. (Class A subordinate voting shares, TSX)

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual: share-based payment costs 68,636k (statement of changes in equity / cash-flow add-back) + withholding taxes remitted on net settlement of PSUs 52,888k (financing activities) = 121.5m. CGI publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed. FY2025 withholding was elevated (FY2024 15.4m, 9M FY2026 23.5m); forward path uses 0.6% of revenue.
inputs.buyback_note: TTM to Jun-2026: Q4 FY2025 490.8m + 9M FY2026 1,386.4m purchases for cancellation (financing activities, cash actually spent). Plus 75.0m 9M FY2026 purchases of shares held in trusts to settle PSUs (SBC settlement, already charged via SBC). CGI is a heavy repurchaser: the flat share count is funded, and over-funded -- the NCIB retires ~6% of the count a year.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted, 208.1m: 182,952,649 Class A + 24,122,758 Class B = 207.08m at 24-Jul-2026 (Q3 FY2026 MD&A s.2.2.3) plus ~1.1m dilution (Q3 diluted weighted 208.85m vs basic 207.77m, treasury method on 2.44m options). Class B (multiple voting) shares are convertible 1:1 into Class A and share identically in dividends and residual value, so the per-share value is on the combined count. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, buybacks are value-neutral capital return.
inputs.fx_note: Statements, flows, WACC and the TSX quote are all CAD: no translation anywhere in this model. Cross-listing parity check at build: NYSE GIB 70.09 USD (2026-10-09T20:00:03Z close) x Yahoo CAD=X 1.4254 USDCAD (2026-10-10T04:21Z) = 99.91 CAD vs observed TSX close 100.08 CAD -- a 0.17% tie confirming one NYSE share = one Class A share. The sibling valuation research/GIB/Reports/GIB_DCF.json is the same CAD model expressed in USD (its fx_rate 0.7019 is USD per CAD at its own build date); its *_cad twins should equal this file's unsuffixed values up to the 0.7019 vs 1/1.4254 = 0.7016 rate drift.
inputs.fy0: TTM to Q3 FY2026 (12 months ended 30-Jun-2026)
inputs.wacc_rationale: CAD build. Canada 10y GoC ~3.4%, ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.95 for a diversified IT-services firm with ~60% recurring managed-services/IP revenue -> cost of equity ~8.2-8.6%. Pre-tax debt ~4.5% (senior unsecured notes; IG rated) -> ~3.3% after tax at ~13% D/V (ex-lease net debt 3.0bn vs equity ~20.8bn CAD). WACC ~7.8%; set 8.25% to reflect organic stagnation not being fully captured in a single base path. Same WACC in all three scenarios: risk is charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked on the discount rate. Identical to GIB: the discount rate belongs to the CAD flows, not to the listing.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. Full lease cash (principal 185.7m TTM: Q4 FY2025 51.4m + 9M FY2026 134.3m; interest ~30m, FY2025 30.5m) charged via lease_cost_pct_path ~1.3% of revenue inside EBIT. Lease liabilities (~680m est. at Jun-2026; 693.5m at Sep-2025) EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (ROU depreciation 138.2m FY2025) so the lease is not charged twice in cash-tax EBIT.
inputs.nci_treatment: None material -- CGI consolidates wholly owned subsidiaries; no NCI deduction.
inputs.net_debt_note: CGI's reported net debt at 30-Jun-2026 is 3,684.0m (Q3 FY2026 MD&A s.4.5): long-term debt and lease liabilities 4,337.1m less cash 625.6m, short-term investments 7.8m, long-term investments 27.7m, plus 8.1m adverse FX derivative on debt. Less lease liabilities ~680m (treatment B) = 3,004m ex-lease. Funds held for clients (1.1bn) excluded: offset by client fund obligations. The US$625m 2021 senior notes mature Sep-2026 (refinanced from the 2.5bn revolver) -- no change to net debt. No filing newer than Q3 FY2026 (Q4 FY2026 results due November 2026), so the Jun-2026 anchors carry over from the GIB build.
inputs.acquisition_treatment: CGI is a serial acquirer ('build and buy'); roughly half of reported growth over a decade was acquired. The revenue paths are ORGANIC plus carry-over of deals already closed and paid (OBS, Comarch Polska, Stratfield -- their cash is in the Jun-2026 net debt). Future acquisitions are assumed NPV-neutral: no acquisition spend is charged and no acquired revenue is projected. Integration costs of acquired businesses are therefore excluded; ~0.5pp of recurring restructuring/cost-optimization is charged in the EBITDA margin.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'Operating company, non-US' + owner-fcf-adaptations: IFRS-16 leases; the dual-currency part does not apply because statements and quote are both CAD). CGI is a mature, profitable, diversified IT services and consulting operating company (managed IT/BPO ~55% of revenue, SI&C ~45%) with no balance-sheet business -- none of the bank/REIT/LIC/holdco rows apply. This is the TSX listing of the company already valued in research/GIB (NYSE, USD quote) on 2026-10-04: a fresh build for THIS ticker (no prior GIB-A.TO DCF, no MEMORY.md entry) but NOT a fresh set of judgments. Every driver path (growth, EBITDA margin, SBC%, lease%, D&A%, capex%, cash tax, WC capture, WACC, terminal growth, exit multiple), every anchor (TTM revenue, net debt, diluted shares, owner FCF) and the scenario weights are inherited verbatim from GIB_Drivers.json -- GIB-A.TO_Metrics.csv was adjudicated to match GIB's CAD figures 1:1, and two share classes of one company cannot carry different business judgments. The only things that differ: current_price is the live TSX CAD quote, quote_currency is CAD, fx_rate is 1.0, and all per-share outputs (IV, entry price, upside, sensitivity) are therefore in CAD with no translation. FY0 is TTM to 30-Jun-2026 so the flows start where the balance sheet ends. Margin anchor: TTM adjusted EBIT 2,695.8m = 16.4% of TTM revenue 16,441.4m; + D&A ~3.7% + SBC ~0.4% = ~20.5% pre-SBC EBITDA, less ~0.5pp recurring restructuring -> 19.9%. Component build gives a year-1 owner-FCF margin ~11.4% vs history FY2024 ~11.5%, FY2025 ~10.3%, TTM ~12.3% on a lease-, SBC- and unlevered-adjusted basis. last_fcf/reported_fcf are FY2025 audited (TTM reported FCF 2,214.0m is flattered by working-capital timing). Interest income not stripped: CGI is net debt, cash is operating.
inputs.sbc_market: SBC is small (~0.4-0.8% of revenue) but non-zero; house and street bands are narrow, not collapsed.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 7.2% vs EPS 5yr CAGR 11.8% (>30% divergence): buybacks retired ~15% of the count since FY2020 so EPS outgrew equity; equity 3yr 12.2% is lifted by retained earnings during an acquisition year. None of the series is organic: revenue CAGRs include ~2-4pp/yr of acquired revenue (Daugherty, BJSS, Novatec, Momentum, Apside in FY2025 alone cost 1.83bn). Selected growth is the organic run-rate judgment (constant-currency growth incl. acquisitions was only 1.3% in Q3 FY2026, 2.1% 9M), not equity CAGR.
historical_growth.notes: Annual FY2020/FY2022 -> FY2025, CAD millions, identical series to GIB (GIB-A.TO_Metrics.csv = GIB_Metrics.csv). Owner FCF series = reported FCF - SBC - equity-award withholding taxes (interest income not stripped, net debt company): FY2020 1,585.8, FY2022 1,438.0, FY2025 1,744.3. Owner-FCF CAGR (6.6% 3yr, 1.9% 5yr) runs ~1pp below reported (7.9%, 2.8%): equity-award withholding jumped in FY2025, so a slightly larger share of reported growth is being paid in stock. FY2020 FCF was flattered by COVID-era collections, depressing the 5yr CAGR. Lease principal is not deducted in these historical CAGRs (it is in the forward build).

base.da_note: D&A ex right-of-use depreciation (~2.85% TTM incl. acquired-intangible amortization), tapering toward capex as acquired client-relationship amortization runs off with no new deals modelled.
base.capex_note: PP&E + intangibles + contract-cost additions: 368.4m FY2025 (2.3%), 376.5m TTM (2.3%).
base.wc_note: IT services: receivables + WIP (DSO 43 days) exceed deferred revenue and payables, so growth consumes cash -- negative capture.
base.tax_note: Guided adjusted ETR 26.0-27.0% (Q3 FY2026 MD&A s.3.8.1); FY2025 cash taxes 603.4m on ~2.24bn pretax ~27%.
base.narrative: Organic growth recovers from ~0% to ~3% as the managed-services backlog (31.8bn, book-to-bill 110% FY2025) converts; margins drift up 0.3pp as recently acquired businesses reach synergy run-rate.

bull.narrative: GenAI is a modernization tailwind, not a deflator: legacy estates (government, banking, utilities) need re-platforming, and CGI's managed-services and IP-based contracts (outcome-priced, not hourly) capture the productivity gain as margin.

bear.narrative: AI coding and agentic tooling compresses billable effort in systems integration (~45% of revenue) faster than new work replaces it; US federal spending cuts and German/European weakness persist; price-downs on renewals erode margin ~1.6pp.

scenario_narratives.base: CGI's organic growth has stalled -- Q3 FY2026 constant-currency growth was 1.3% including acquisitions, so organic is roughly flat -- but the order backlog sits at a record 31.8bn CAD (~1.9x revenue) and FY2025 book-to-bill was 110%. Base case: organic growth recovers to ~3% by year 3 as managed-services and government (U.K., Canada, U.S. state/local) wins convert, offset by continued softness in Germany and commercial SI&C. Adjusted EBIT margin edges from 16.4% to ~16.7% as BJSS/Daugherty/Comarch integration synergies land. Cash taxes at the guided ~26.5%. Capital return continues (6%/yr buyback, 0.68 CAD dividend) but is value-neutral in the model.
scenario_narratives.bull: Generative AI drives a multi-year legacy-modernization cycle in CGI's core verticals (government, financial services, utilities), where data-sovereignty and regulated-workload requirements favour a local-presence operator over offshore pure-plays. CGI's IP-based and outcome-priced managed-services mix lets it keep AI productivity gains as margin rather than pass them through as fewer billable hours. Organic growth reaches ~5% and adjusted EBIT margin ~18%.
scenario_narratives.bear: AI-assisted development and testing deflate the labour-hour economics of SI&C, and clients reprice managed-services renewals to share the productivity gain. US federal (12.7% of 9M FY2026 revenue) remains under spending pressure, Germany stays weak, and organic revenue declines for two years before stabilizing at ~2% growth. Adjusted EBIT margin falls toward ~14.5% -- still profitable and cash generative, so the business does not hit the terminal floor, but the market keeps IT-services multiples compressed (11x exit). A CEO transition (effective May 2026) and ROIC slipping from 16.0% to 13.4% on the acquisition cadence add execution risk to the 'buy' half of the strategy.
scenario_narratives.unchanged_note: First DCF for the GIB-A.TO ticker, but every driver path, anchor and weight is carried verbatim from research/GIB/Reports/GIB_Drivers.json (2026-10-04). Nothing was re-judged: no new CGI filing has landed since that build, and the two listings are the same shares. What would move these paths is the Q4 FY2026 release (November 2026): FY2026 organic growth versus the ~0% run-rate, FY2027 ETR and margin guidance, the Sep-2026 balance sheet (post US$625m note refinancing) and the year-end share count. When that lands, update GIB and GIB-A.TO together from one set of drivers.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because organic growth is already ~0 and AI-driven deflation of billable services is a live, sector-wide de-rating thesis, not a tail risk. Base held at 50% on a record backlog and 110% book-to-bill. Bull cut to 25% because it needs two independent things (AI as net demand tailwind AND CGI retaining the productivity gain as margin). Same weights as GIB.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Organic owner-FCF valuation of a mature IT services compounder, expressed in the currency it reports in. Acquisitions treated as NPV-neutral (neither the spend nor the acquired revenue is modelled); buybacks are the capital return, not a value source. The value question is whether CGI's ~11% owner-FCF margin on a ~16bn CAD revenue base can grow at all organically in an AI-deflation world -- the current TSX price embeds roughly the bear-to-base range. This file and research/GIB are one valuation in two quote currencies; a divergence between them beyond the USDCAD move is a build error, not a view.
key_risks_to_valuation: AI deflation of billable SI&C effort (bear axis) -- the single largest driver of the scenario spread
US federal government exposure (12.7% of 9M FY2026 revenue) to procurement cuts
Acquisition discipline: the model assumes deals are NPV-neutral; overpaying would destroy value the model does not charge

No FX translation in this listing's per-share values (CAD model, CAD quote), but ~75% of revenue is earned outside Canada so the CAD flows themselves carry translation exposure through the operating lines
Lease liability at Jun-2026 estimated (~680m) from the debt+lease total; exact figure in the Q3 interim statements

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (GIB-A.TO, TSX) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 83.34-131.97 CAD. Cross-listing parity against NYSE GIB and CAD=X from the same API, documented in inputs.fx_note.
data_sources.financials: GIB-A.TO_Metrics.csv / GIB-A.TO.duckdb core_metrics + kpis (FY2014-Q3 FY2026), adjudicated to match GIB_Metrics.csv 1:1 (same CAD statements); FY2025 Annual Report (MD&A s.4.1, Note 24); Q3 FY2026 MD&A (s.2.2, 3.8, 4.1, 4.2, 4.5).
data_sources.qualitative: research/GIB/Reports/GIB_Analysis.json (bull/bear cases, risks) plus Q3 FY2026 and FY2025 MD&A segment commentary; no separate GIB-A.TO analysis exists and none is needed -- same company.

sibling_valuation.relationship: Same model, same CAD drivers, USD quote. GIB's intrinsic_value_cad / weighted_iv_cad twins are the values to compare against this file's unsuffixed CAD outputs; GIB's unsuffixed USD values are this file's values divided by USDCAD.
sibling_valuation.sanity_check_note: GIB's hand-recomputed CAD multiples (sanity_check_note in GIB_Drivers.json: historical P/E 17.6-23.8x avg 20.7x, EV/EBITDA 10.7-14.9x avg 12.4x; base IV implied P/E 18.4x, EV/EBITDA 10.3x) apply to this listing directly and without the fx-direction caveat, since price, EPS and IV are all CAD here.
